nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the Boolean AND of all coordinates: it sends $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ to true exactly when $x_i$ is true for every $i < n$. In dimension $0$ it is constantly true.
nodes.title: All-true function

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the set of functions $x : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. It represents $\{-1, 1\}^n$, with true standing for $1$ and false for $-1$.
nodes.title: Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $c$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at the empty set of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $c$. This includes dimension $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Empty Fourier coefficient of a constant function

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the character $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$ on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $1$, that is, $\widehat{\chi_S}(S) = 1$.
nodes.title: A character's own Fourier coefficient

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the empty set is the uniform mean of $f$: $\hat f(\emptyset) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.
nodes.title: The empty Fourier coefficient is the mean

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the identically zero function on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of the zero function

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$. That is, $\hat f(S)$ is the uniform expectation of $f \chi_S$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficient on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: The all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $2$, $(x_0, x_1) \mapsto x_0 \wedge x_1$, has Boolean degree $2$; that is, its real multilinear extension has total degree $2$.
nodes.title: The two-bit AND has Boolean degree two

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every Boolean value $b$, the constant function $x \mapsto b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have Boolean degree zero

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $i < n$, the coordinate projection $x \mapsto x_i$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $1$.
nodes.title: Coordinate projections have Boolean degree one

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, and read true as $1$ and false as $0$. The Boolean degree of $f$ is the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$: the real multilinear polynomial in $n$ variables that takes the value $f(x)$ at every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.title: Boolean degree

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has exactly $2^n$ points.
nodes.title: Number of points of the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, indexed by $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Its cube basis polynomial is the real polynomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \ell_i$ in the variables $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$, where $\ell_i = X_i$ if $x_i$ is true and $\ell_i = 1 - X_i$ if $x_i$ is false. Reading true as $1$ and false as $0$, it is the Lagrange basis polynomial of $x$ on the grid $\{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.title: Lagrange basis polynomial of a cube point

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_\emptyset$ of the empty set of coordinates satisfies $\chi_\emptyset(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: The empty Fourier character is constant one

nodes.summary: For every $n$, every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies $\chi_S(x) \cdot \chi_S(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: Fourier characters square to one

nodes.summary: For every $n$, every coordinate $i$ and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_{\{i\}}$ of the singleton $\{i\}$ satisfies $\chi_{\{i\}}(x) = \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.
nodes.title: Singleton Fourier characters are coordinate signs

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of coordinates among $n$, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ is the real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates given by $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.
nodes.title: Fourier character on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: The sign $\sigma(\text{false})$ of the Boolean value false equals $-1$.
nodes.title: Sign of false

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ satisfies $\sigma(b) \cdot \sigma(b) = 1$.
nodes.title: Coordinate signs square to one

nodes.summary: The sign $\sigma(\text{true})$ of the Boolean value true equals $1$.
nodes.title: Sign of true

nodes.summary: The sign of a Boolean value $b$ is the real number $\sigma(b)$ given by $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.
nodes.title: Sign of a Boolean coordinate

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$; this order identifies subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$. A point $x$ of that cube decodes to the subset $\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$; this inverts the encoding of subsets of $E$ as cube points.
nodes.title: Decoding a cube point as a subset

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$. Encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point $x_T$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when $e_j \in T$, and decode a point $x$ as the subset $\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$. Then for every subset $T \subseteq E$, decoding $x_T$ gives back $T$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts encoding

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and identify $y$ with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the cube basis polynomial of $x$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Lagrange basis polynomials on the cube are point indicators

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $y$ be a point of the cube, identified with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the real multilinear extension of $f$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $f(y)$ is true and $0$ if $f(y)$ is false.
nodes.title: The multilinear extension agrees with its function on the cube

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point $x_T$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when $e_j \in T$. For all subsets $S, T \subseteq E$,
nodes.title: Subset characters agree with cube characters

nodes.summary: For finite sets $S$ and $T$, the Fourier character of $S$ at $T$ is the real number $\chi_S(T) = (-1)^{|S \cap T|}$.
nodes.title: Fourier character on finite sets

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and decode a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ as the subset $D(x) = \{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$. Let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$ and let $S \subseteq E$. Then the Fourier coefficient…
nodes.title: Subset Fourier coefficients agree with cube Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For a finite subset $S$ of $\iota$, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ over $E$ is
nodes.title: Fourier coefficient on the subsets of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$,
nodes.title: Fourier inversion on the subsets of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. Then
nodes.title: Plancherel identity on the subsets of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If $f$ has Fourier degree at most $d$, then $f$ has Fourier degree at most $e$.
nodes.title: Fourier degree bounds are monotone

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $g$ be the real function with $g(x) = 1$ if $f(x)$ is true and $g(x) = 0$ otherwise. Then $g$ has Fourier degree at most the Boolean degree of $f$: every Fourier coefficient $\hat g(S)$ with $|S|$ greater than the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$ vanishes.
nodes.title: Fourier degree is at most Boolean degree

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \ge n$ be a natural number. Then $f$ has Fourier degree at most $d$.
nodes.title: Fourier degree is at most the dimension

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the zero function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Fourier degree at most $d$.
nodes.title: The zero function satisfies every Fourier degree bound

nodes.summary: A real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Fourier degree at most a natural number $d$ when its Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ vanishes for every set $S$ of coordinates with $|S| > d$.
nodes.title: Fourier degree at most $d$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the real multilinear extension of the AND function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ (true exactly when every coordinate is true) is the monomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i$.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of the AND function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every Boolean value $b$, the real multilinear extension of the constant function $b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the constant polynomial $1$ if $b$ is true and the constant polynomial $0$ if $b$ is false.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of a constant function

nodes.summary: For every coordinate $i$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, the real multilinear extension of the projection $x \mapsto x_i$ is the variable $X_i$.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of a coordinate projection

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and read each coordinate and each value as $1$ for true and $0$ for false. The real multilinear extension of $f$ is the polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}]$
nodes.title: Multilinear extension

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in the fixed order $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$ used to encode subsets of $E$ as points of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$ and every coordinate $j < m$, the $j$-th coordinate of the point encoding $T$ is true if $e_j \notin T$ and false if $e_j \in T$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of an encoded subset

nodes.summary: For a finite set $E$ with $n = |E|$ elements, fix a bijection $e$ from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (an enumeration of $E$, chosen noncanonically). This is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ that sends $T$ to the point $x$ with $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$, for every $a \in E$.
nodes.title: Subsets of a finite set as points of the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For a finite set $E$, this is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the functions $b$ from $E$ to $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ given by $b(a) = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $b(a) = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the set $\{a \in E : b(a) = \mathrm{false}\}$.
nodes.title: Subsets of a finite set as indicator functions

nodes.summary: For finite sets $S \subseteq E$ with $n = |E|$, let $e$ be the fixed bijection from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the enumeration of $E$ used to identify subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$). The reindexed set is the image $e(S) = \{e(a) : a \in S\}$, a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Reindexing a subset as a set of coordinates

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
